limits: Windows timer granularity: without raising system timer resolution (e.g., timeBeginPeriod), WaitForSingleObject(r->stopping, 2) typically sleeps at the active system tick (~15.625 ms by default unless another process lowered it) rather than 2 ms, and GetTickCount64() advances at the same tick granularity (~2000 ms + up to 1 tick); actual cadence is observable via early_count and [first_early_qpc, last_early_qpc] in EARLY_FLUSH.

If the very first FlushTraceW fails (status != 0), first_early_qpc is recorded before break while early_count and last_early_qpc stay 0 (harmless diagnostic asymmetry on a failing exit-4 run); catastrophic 5s drain-timeout ExitProcess(4) paths omit EARLY_FLUSH.

When timer resolution is low (e.g., 1 ms), up to ~500 flushes/sec during the 2 s window increases ETW buffer seal frequency for non-empty buffers (including system-wide DXGI 42/43 and DxgKrnl 166/184 traffic); overflow remains bounded and fail-closed via RealTimeBuffersLost.

Pre-bind gap remains 10 ms polling before client-pid binds, and any observed negative result (no event consumed/ACKed before public Present return) applies only to the measured run/cadence and does not generalize across all boots or timer resolutions.
CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION requires Windows 10 1803+ (satisfied by WDDM 2.6 / 1903+, fails closed with exit 3 on older OS builds).
early_deadline still uses GetTickCount64() (~15.6 ms system tick granularity), so the nominal 2000 ms high-resolution window boundary is quantized by up to ~1 tick.
A >=250 ms scheduler stall or preemption while waiting on pulse triggers WAIT_TIMEOUT and aborts fail-closed with ERROR_TIMEOUT.

Achieving ~2 ms (~500 Hz) actual flush cadence increases ETW buffer seal rate whenever non-empty system-wide DXGI 42/43 or DxgKrnl 166/184 events are present; overflow remains bounded and fail-closed via RealTimeBuffersLost.

Pre-bind polling remains 10 ms (WaitForSingleObject), catastrophic 5 s drain-timeout ExitProcess(4) skips EARLY_TIMER stderr output, and single-run timing results do not generalize across all boots or system loads.

Directory name matching uses case-sensitive wcsncmp/wcscmp, so the staging directory must use exact-case WinPresentLive-<lowercase-12-hex>; ancestor directories above it are not checked for reparse points.

Standalone invocation with --local-blt-receipt gates exit code on r->journal_status rather than (local_blt && !r->journal_sequence); requiring a persisted 166 record relies on the paired stream_receiver.py (which requires DxgKrnl 166 before DRAIN/DONE) and downstream blt-receipt.bin verification.

Because CREATE_NEW runs at startup before ETW delivery, runs that fail before DxgKrnl 166 or during WriteFile leave an empty/partial blt-receipt.bin in WinPresentLive-<nonce> alongside exit code 4 and LOCAL_BLT diagnostics.

persist_blt runs WriteFile + FlushFileBuffers synchronously under output_lock on the ETW consumer thread (at most once); a prolonged storage stall delays wire output and could trigger RealTimeBuffersLost (fail-closed).

FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH + FlushFileBuffers flushes through Windows NTFS/volume caches (including the file's NTFS metadata transaction), while actual power-loss media durability still depends on the Switch storage driver/eMMC/SD honoring flush/FUA; catastrophic 5 s drain-timeout ExitProcess(4) skips LOCAL_BLT stderr output.
